title: The Dhamaal Boys Chase a Mountain of Gold. Dhamaal 4 Lands July 10 and It Has No Intention of Growing Up.
excerpt: Ajay Devgn, Arshad Warsi, Riteish Deshmukh and Jaaved Jaaferi reunite for a ₹200-crore treasure hunt — and after two songs and a trailer, the diaspora's most reliable summer comedy is back, loud and unbothered.
body:
The play button arrived with a dare. "Theek saamne, aapko woh play button dikh raha hai? Haan, usse daba dijiye" — see that play button right in front of you? Go on, press it. That is how **T-Series** unveiled the **Dhamaal 4** trailer, and the cheekiness is the whole point. This franchise has never pretended to be clever. It has only ever promised to be loud, and on that promise it has never once defaulted.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=IG-eByZdz6Y</youtube>

The trailer dropped a wild treasure hunt straight into your lap: a mountain of gold somewhere out there, and four grown men who will faceplant their way toward it across jungles, animals, accidents and a rapid-fire chain of mistaken identities. **Ajay Devgn** anchors it the way he always has — the straight man who is somehow the most ridiculous of all — while **Arshad Warsi**, **Riteish Deshmukh** and **Jaaved Jaaferi** slot back into their slapstick rhythm like nineteen years never passed. There is a line in the footage that doubles as a mission statement: "Listen, brother. This is a family film. None of that is allowed here." Translation — leave your good taste at the door, bring the whole household, and don't overthink it.

https://x.com/TSeries/status/2068245074375528933

> "Watch the biggest family entertainer #Dhamaal4 in cinemas worldwide from 10th July!" — T-Series, official trailer

Let's be honest about what this is. The trailer is pure masala chaos, not smart comedy, and the VFX in places looks exactly like a film betting its money on movement rather than polish. But that has always been the deal with **Dhamaal**. The 2007 original ran on nothing but timing and an ensemble willing to look stupid on cue. **Double Dhamaal** (2011) surprised the trade with a healthy opening. **Total Dhamaal** (2019) detonated — a ₹16.50 crore opening day on its way to ₹154 crore lifetime. Director **Indra Kumar** knows the formula isn't broken, so he hasn't fixed it. He's just made it bigger, mounting Dhamaal 4 on a reported ₹200-crore canvas and turning the trailer launch at Imagicaa into an adventure-park spectacle to match.

The music rollout has been just as relentless. After the high-energy **'Chatni'**, the makers dropped **'Qeher'**, a **Guru Randhawa** banger that hands the Dhamaal boys an infectious hook step and lets them look their quirky best, with **Ketika Sharma** in a special appearance. The soundtrack is a who's-who of chart-machine producers — Tanishk Bagchi, Aditya Dev, Sanju Rathod, Guru Randhawa — which tells you exactly which audience this is courting. This is a film engineered to play loud in a packed hall and louder on a wedding speaker six months later.

The ensemble is where Dhamaal 4 gets greedy, in the best way. Alongside the core four and **Sanjay Mishra**, the makers have folded in **Esha Gupta**, **Sanjeeda Shaikh**, **Anjali Anand**, **Upendra Limaye**, **Vijay Patkar** and a scene-stealing **Ravi Kishan** — the kind of stacked roster that exists purely so every five minutes has a new face to bounce a gag off. It is comedy by volume, and that strategy has carried this franchise for nearly two decades.

For the diaspora, the timing is the gift. Dhamaal 4 releases **in cinemas worldwide on July 10, 2026** — a same-day global rollout, which means desi families in New Jersey, Toronto and Southall get the AMC and Cineworld matinee at the same moment as Mumbai. This is also the film that blinked first in July's traffic jam: originally locked for July 17, the makers preponed it a week to July 10 once **Alpha** claimed July 3, dodging a brutal screen war and handing fans the laugh riot earlier. Smart counter-programming — let the spy thrillers and mythological epics fight over prestige; Dhamaal will quietly sell the popcorn.

Will it be good? Almost beside the point. Dhamaal has always been review-proof, the cinematic equivalent of comfort food you're slightly embarrassed to love. The audience buzz out of the trailer is already calling it "paisa vasool," and for a homesick NRI weekend, that's the only review that matters. Press play. You knew you were going to.
author: Diaspora Desk
